brief: An aluminium cantilever bracket: a 60 mm long, 20 mm wide, 6 mm thick bar fixed at one end by two 5 mm bolt holes 15 mm apart near that end. A load of 150 N pushes straight down on the free end. It must have a safety factor of at least 2.

intent.summary: An aluminium cantilever bracket with a 60 mm long, 20 mm wide, and 6 mm thick bar. It is fixed at one end by two 5 mm bolt holes 15 mm apart near that end. A load of 150 N is applied straight down on the free end, and it must have a safety factor of at least 2.
implied: the free end of the bracket
the bolt holes are near the end
the load is applied straight down
unstated: the magnitude and direction of the load on the arm
the material grade of the bracket
the operating temperature of the bracket
the dimensions that are load-bearing for the design's function
risk_signals: part of a vehicle or of regulated equipment

requirements.statement: The length of the cantilever bracket shall be 60 mm.
The width of the cantilever bracket shall be 20 mm.
The thickness of the cantilever bracket shall be 6 mm.
There shall be two bolt holes near the end of the cantilever bracket.
The part shall keep a safety factor of at least 2 against yield in bending at its support.
The part shall have 2 open holes of 5 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief sizes and counts these holes.

requirements.statement: an aluminium cantilever bracket: a 60 mm long, 20 mm wide, 6 mm thick bar fixed at one end by two 5 mm bolt holes 15 mm apart near that end.

assumptions.statement: The 150 N load acts straight down on the free end of the cantilever bracket.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A larger, dynamic or differently placed load invalidates every margin computed from this one.

assumptions.statement: The aluminium is aluminium_6061_t6 (aluminium_6061_t6), the only grade of it Forge knows.
assumptions.rationale: The brief names the family, not the grade, and the safety factor depends on which grade it is.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Grades of aluminium differ in yield strength several times over; every margin computed here would be wrong.

notes: `feature_count:bolt_hole:near_end` names no feature kind, so it was read as `feature_count:hole:bolt`.

REQ_NEAR_END_BOLT_HOLE_COUNT counted `bolt` 2.0 as a bound; the brief states the count -- "an aluminium cantilever bracket: a 60 mm long, 20 mm wide, 6 mm thick bar fixed at one end by two 5 mm bolt holes 15 mm apart near that end" -- so it is exactly that many.

added REQ_HOLES_5MM: the brief states 2 open holes of 5 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLE_SPACING at 15 mm: the brief places the holes with it -- "an aluminium cantilever bracket: a 60 mm long, 20 mm wide, 6 mm thick bar fixed at one end by two 5 mm bolt holes 15 mm apart near that end" -- and no requirement carried it.

REQ_SF_BEARING measured `safety_factor:bearing`, and the brief describes a bar held at one end and loaded at the other, with no pin in a bore: its margin is the bending at the support. Now `safety_factor:bending`; the threshold is unchanged.

ASM_DESIGN_LOAD states the load in words -- "The 150 N load acts straight down on the free end of the cantilever bracket." -- and carried no value, so no margin could have been computed from it. Its value is now 150 N, the force the brief states.

added ASM_MATERIAL_GRADE: the brief says `aluminium`, the safety factor depends on the grade, and `aluminium_6061_t6` is the only one Forge knows. The margin is computed for it, and the part is not released until that is approved.

answer.rationale: The brief describes a cantilever bracket with specific dimensions and requirements. The part is designed to be a cantilever bracket with a 60 mm long, 20 mm wide, and 6 mm thick bar. It is fixed at one end by two 5 mm bolt holes 15 mm apart near that end. A load of 150 N is applied straight down on the free end, and it must have a safety factor of at least 2.
